Can you build a legitimate video game business on prompts? Meta thinks so
"This is the modern way to make video games," says Meta Horizon VP Saxs Persson
Christopher Dring
10 hours ago
Listen now on Apple , Spotify or YouTube
In This Edition,
Meta Horizon VP Saxs Persson on…
UGC vs traditional games
AI games as a business
Google vs Roblox vs Meta
Last month, Meta revealed Horizon Studio and Horizon Create.
They’re AI-powered game making tools where people can make games using text prompts and then publish them directly onto mobile and social feeds, including Instagram and Facebook.
“The developer vision is to break down the barriers [to game making] as much as we can using modern tools,” begins Saxs Persson, who is VP of Horizon at Meta. “AI happens to be an extraordinary accelerator for certain things that have been very difficult. A good game is iteration. If we can buy more iteration with powerful tools that make it faster, more precise, and so more people can iterate, we should expect more interesting games, because it doesn’t cost as much. That’s the developer vision.
Persson is a veteran of the user-generated content space. At Microsoft, he was executive producer on the game creation title Project Spark, before taking a leadership role on Minecraft. From there he went to Epic Games, where he was responsible for Unreal Editor for Fortnite, and enabling other creators to build games within that ecosystem (including LEGO Fortnite).
Persson worked on LEGO Fortnite
“‘User-generated content’ is not a great phrase for what this really is,” he says. “These are smaller developers making games that people play for billions of hours. There’s a whole generation growing up where this is just part of how you play games. And it’s a new generation of developers showing a modern take on how to make games and what a game should do to be successful.
“From my perspective, it still complements traditional game-making. I have the same respect for traditional games that are more crafted as a statement from the team, versus user-generated content, which is often more measuring yourselves in how people feel when playing your game, and about that direct communication between the community and the game maker.”
Meta vs Google vs Roblox
Saxs Persson, Meta
Horizon isn’t the only operator in this space. There are numerous start-ups where people can build games via prompts, and then there’s major players like Roblox and Google.
Persson believes Meta has advantages over its competitors in that it’s been built from scratch for this. “We don’t sit on 20 years of very opinionated codebases and licenses,” he says.
It also has ambitions to go far broader. “Meta understands scale. It’s a company that doesn’t blink when you say a billion people. It just thinks, ‘Why not two?’ That’s the type of company it is.”
But one of the key differentiators between Horizon and something like Roblox is that the various games can look and feel completely different from one another.
“There’s not a particular look,” Persson tells us. “The character is your character, the environment is your environment, the style is your style. We’re very welcoming to ship to the widest possible audience exactly the thing that you want to make, in the style you want to make it. There’s nothing quite like that.
“Roblox is very opinionated from an artistic perspective. Minecraft the same thing, Fortnite the same thing. Fortnite on mobile is not at scale. Roblox is certainly at scale but it’s hard to imagine a rich artistic look compatible with how Roblox went about building its engine. We’re trying to fade into the background to provide the components for the games to be the center, and Meta to be the platform that helps the games get there. Similar to YouTube. YouTube is not opinionated about what content they have. They serve the content that matches up with the viewers’ interest, and gets out of the way.
“And from an IP perspective, that’s the other differentiator, this is a good place to be. You can make the thing that represents your IP accurately in the way that you would want to make it and distributed to the widest possible audience, with very little friction and cost.”
Is it a business opportunity?
I’ve told this story before, but a 12-year-old family member once showed me a Wipeout-like racing game he’d made. He coded it himself, but the assets were all AI-generated. He was so happy as we all played it together over Christmas, and it was a joy to witness. There are clearly deep concerns about the technology, but I can see the benefits, too.
“People that make games are like circus horses,” Persson says. “We smell the sawdust, and we walk in circles, because it’s so addicting to make a game, to make something out of nothing and have people find joy in playing it. It’s the most satisfying thing I can think of. Giving that feeling to more people, I have a hard time thinking that that’s nothing but a positive thing.”
Persson says this isn’t about one-shotting games. It’s about iteration, testing, trying and repeating. Google Playground is similar and even has a partnership with Unity, too, to add even more manual control over the games being built.
But we’re a business publication, and the question remains, are vibe-coded and prompt-based games a legitimate business opportunity for professional game teams?
“It’s absolutely a business opportunity,” Persson insists. “Is it a business opportunity for a triple-A team to switch to this platform right now? No. There’s a particular flavor to it that we’ll start with, but it’s still a business opportunity.
“I spend a lot of time with new indie teams. My pride lies in whether I can inspire people to take that first step, make that first level, and get a group together that’s going to make a magical game. Those are very much business opportunities. We should measure ourselves in our ability to enable people to be entrepreneurs on the platform.
“We should measure ourselves in our ability to enable people to be entrepreneurs on the platform”
“In many ways, it complements the traditional game industry. I don’t think it directly steps on top of it or anything. My controversial opinion is that this is the modern way of making games, which is faster iterations, closer connection to your community, and a higher tolerance for experimentation.”
Persson points to Spotify as a platform that simultaneously ruined the music industry, and opened it up so everyone could be a musician. He thinks video games “can do better than that”, by preserving the premium, AAA space while expanding the UGC sector.
But AI poses plenty of other concerns, such as IP protection. In my research for this article, one investor told me to check out AI game platform Spawn.co. And the first thing I saw when booting it up was an unofficial Pokémon game.
“You can’t operate a platform if you don’t observe all the basic safeguards for preserving intellectual property,” Persson notes. “There are things you can do above and beyond that. My goal is that this will be a first-rate place for IP, because I really think that matters from a player perspective. You want the legitimate experience that feels exactly like the thing. I worked a lot with LEGO and Star Wars in my past, and I certainly have an appreciation for how precise a [company] feels their IP needs to be represented.”
And the other challenge is making sure users, particularly younger users, are protected. This is something Roblox has been wrestling with in recent history.
“The industry is growing up, and you really have to be on the A-game to operate a global platform. The global regulatory landscape is not the easiest to navigate, but it’s there for a reason. For us to develop trust long term is directly proportional to the integrity of the platform, from a content and age perspective, and in terms of business practices.”
We’re entering an unknown future when it comes to game making. The optimists will tell you that AI tools will just unlock a new generation of game makers, potentially uncover new types of experiences that can grow the industry, and ultimately complement the traditional business. The pessimists will tell you it’ll flood the market with low quality content, make it significantly harder for traditional developers to compete, drive piracy, and result in a sharp decrease in the number of professional game makers.
Persson, perhaps inevitably, is in the former camp.
“Every year we take more steps to remove more moats, to democratize the act of making games,” he concludes. “I have no illusion everybody’s going to make a game, but I do agonize over the fact that the people that really have a game in them ought to have the option. So, ten years from now, I want to imagine that the making and publishing of games are democratized to a point that the best games can find a platform and an audience. Ten years from now humans are still making games like they’ve always been making games. Ten years from now a good idea is still a good idea. Ten years from now you’re iterating on your game for six months, but the tools surrounding it will just make it faster, easier, more fun to measure.
“And I think there’ll be a whole new category of games where the agent sits in the runtime, which really energizes me. I want to bring about not just a different way to make a game, but a different way to playit, and we’re just getting to that. From my perspective, that’s where we can really bring innovation to the industry, which is to allow reasoning to influence how the game develops.”

title: 2026年9月成功出海的中国手游
author: Sensor Tower
text:
Sensor Tower 发布2026年9月中国手游海外市场收入及下载量排行榜！详细榜单变化如下。
特别说明：榜单仅统计应⽤商店IAP预估值，不包括⼴告变现、中国大陆地区及第三方安卓渠道收入。
9月出海手游收入榜
2026年9月中国手游出海收入Top 30榜单中，柠檬微趣旗下《Gossip Harbor: Merge & Story》稳居榜首；点点互动旗下三款产品包揽第2至第4名，继续展现其在海外手游市场的强势表现；米哈游旗下《崩坏：星穹铁道》与《原神》排名均有所上升；三七互娱旗下《Last Asylum: Plague》海外收入再创新高，今年5月上线的游戏《Z Route: Redemption》则首次入榜，成为本月值得关注的产品之一。
点点互动旗下二合手游《Tasty Travels: Merge Game》9月位列中国手游出海收入榜第4名，根据Sensor Tower数据估算，该游戏在截止发稿日，累计海外收入已突破4.5亿美元，也体现了点点互动在 SLG 以外的产品竞争力。9月，游戏围绕秋季主题推出岛屿装饰活动，持续提供新的装饰收集目标。
米哈游旗下《原神》迎来全球上线六周年，海外收入环比增长17%，日本和美国分别贡献本月出海收入的38%与18%。9月23日，7.1版本“往冥府的安魂歌”开启，新五星角色薇斯纳（风）与沃雅妮莎（水）登场，魔神任务第七章第三、四幕进一步推进至冬主线。周年庆福利与新版本内容同期上线，游戏收入于9月23日达到当月峰值。
沐瞳科技旗下《Mobile Legends: Bang Bang》9月迎来十周年，游戏以“ALL IN MLBB”为主题，通过周年纪念战令、限定皮肤及回顾游戏历程的专属活动，增强玩家的周年参与感。9月15日起，Masha、Clint、Brody 等英雄回归，为老玩家带来熟悉角色的新体验。市场方面，9月印度尼西亚、马来西亚和土耳其等地区收入均有所增长，游戏当月海外收入环比增长4%。
三七互娱旗下《Last Asylum: Plague》9月海外收入突破2600万美元，再创新高，核心市场美国、德国和日本月收入均刷新纪录。9月，游戏在全球4X策略手游收入榜中上升一位至第6名，超越 Top Games 旗下《Evony》，进一步提升其在SLG细分赛道中的竞争力。运营方面，9月下旬的中秋主题活动“Full Moon Night”融合战令、抽取、月饼收集、限时兑换及小游戏，丰富玩家参与体验。根据 Sensor Tower 旗下Pathmatics 数字广告洞察，9月该游戏在美国市场的YouTube渠道 广告展示量约2.4亿次，环比大幅增长，成为当月展示量最高的渠道。
三七互娱 旗下《Z Route: Redemption》9月首次入围中国手游出海收入榜 Top 30。该游戏于5月上线 App Store，8月登陆 Google Play；9月收入近半来自美国，德国、英国和法国合计贡献约20%。玩法上，《Z Route》以末世丧尸为背景，结合数值门选择、跑酷射击等关卡玩法，以及基地建设、英雄养成等SLG元素，成为继《Puzzles & Survival》之后，三七互娱在SLG产品矩阵的又一成功布局。
9月出海手游收入增长榜
2026年9月中国手游出海收入增长榜显示，多款游戏的收入增长与海外版本上线、区域市场拓展有关。益世界旗下《疯狂水世界》位居榜首；Joy Games旗下《Duck Survival》凭借繁中版与韩版相继上线，收入环比增长约140%；点点互动旗下《Lordrush》延续上线后的增长势头；与此同时，哔哩哔哩旗下《闪耀吧！噜咪》凭借上线后的收入爆发进入增长榜前十，《崩坏：星穹铁道》、《原神》与《恋与深空》等成熟产品也实现不同程度的收入增长。

title: 2026年7月中国手游发行商全球收入排行榜

text:
Sensor Tower 商店情报平台显示，2026年7月共38个中国厂商入围全球手游发行商收入榜 TOP 100，合计吸金23亿美元，占本期全球 TOP 100手游发行商收入42.6%。
特别说明：本报告仅统计发行商收入，应用数据包含 App Store 与 Google Play 的综合预估值，不包含第三方 Android 应用商店数据（中国大陆市场仅统计 iOS 端）。本报告中的预估数据不代表发行商财务报表确认收入。
中国手游发行商收入 TOP 30
7月中国手游 Top 5发行商收入均过亿（美元），腾讯、网易、米哈游实现两位数增长，其中米哈游收入环比大增71%，增幅位居 Top 30发行商前列；沐瞳科技、心动网络、Modo Global 等多家发行商在暑期内容与活动推动下实现收入显著增长。
腾讯 持续蝉联7月全球手游发行商收入榜冠军。本期稳健表现主要得益于《王者荣耀》、《和平精英》及《PUBG MOBILE（绝地求生）》等头部主力的全线增长。与此同时，腾讯在7月密集推出了体感音舞手游《舞力全开：派对》与开放世界生存游戏《失控进化》等新作，丰富暑期档产品矩阵。
《王者荣耀》7月运营活动排期紧凑，高频联动推高流水。月初上线“西行封妖记”系列第二批皮肤；月中借“墨子-迪迦奥特曼”珍品传说祈愿引爆 IP 联动热度；月末则通过牛年限定祈愿返场及公孙离星传说等活动进一步丰富付费内容。密集的商业化排期叠加暑期活跃红利，推动该作7月收入环比大涨35%，全球吸金约2亿美元。
《和平精英》自7月3日起长期稳居中国大陆 iOS 游戏畅销榜 Top 3。其暑期版本“夏日探险”的长线转化助推游戏于7月10日触及月内收入峰值，下旬接档的《吞噬星空》长线 IP 联动则延续了活跃度。与此同时，吃鸡游戏在海外同样表现亮眼，《PUBG MOBILE》7月在美国、沙特阿拉伯及日本等主要市场的收入与下载量均实现同步增长。
网易 稳居中国手游发行商排行榜第4名。旗下《蛋仔派对》7月收入表现突出，自2月以来再度超越《梦幻西游》，重夺网易旗下手游收入冠军。在四周年庆典、<超燃>系列玩法更新、热门 IP “Flying DongDong” 联动以及S32新赛季“惊魂盛典季”的多维驱动下，该游戏在7月暑期展现出强劲的商业化爆发力。7月10日，游戏全球单日收入跃升至260万美元，创下年内单日流水第二高峰；并于10日至11日连续两天跻身中国 iOS 手游畅销榜第3名，刷新年内最好成绩。Sensor Tower 数据显示，截至7月31日，该作全球累计收入已超过7.7亿美元。

title: 2026年9月中国手游发行商全球收入排行榜
author: Sensor Tower
text:
Sensor Tower 商店情报平台显示，2026年9月共36个中国厂商入围全球手游发行商收入榜 TOP 100，合计吸金20亿美元，占本期全球 TOP 100手游发行商收入40.4%。
特别说明：本报告仅统计发行商收入，应用数据包含 App Store 与 Google Play 的综合预估值，不包含第三方 Android 应用商店数据（中国大陆市场仅统计 iOS 端）。本报告中的预估数据不代表发行商财务报表确认收入。
中国手游发行商收入TOP 30
9月，中国手游发行商榜单头部格局高度稳固，前七名发行商排名均保持不变，腾讯继续稳居榜首。中腰部发行商表现更为突出，哔哩哔哩收入环比增长36%，排名上升7位；Joy Games 排名提升10位，成为本月排名上升幅度较大的发行商之一。此外，益世界、游酷盛世和露珠游戏重回榜单。
莉莉丝 整体收入自4月起连续增长，9月发行商整体收入创年内新高，进一步巩固其在中国手游发行商收入榜中的竞争位置。《Clash of Critters》（《塔塔冒险队》）贡献了主要收入增量，9月收入占发行商总收入的比例提升至42%。更值得关注的是，该游戏8月收入刚刚超越同厂商旗下《万国觉醒》，至9月收入已达到后者的约两倍，领先优势迅速扩大。随着游戏8月底在中国台湾和韩国市场收入提升，以及9月4日登陆中国大陆 iOS，游戏持续扩大用户覆盖。9月，中国大陆、日本、美国和中国台湾合计贡献收入68%，多区域市场共同支撑其收入表现。
灵犀互娱 9月手游收入环比增长33%，排名上升4位至第9名。根据 Sensor Tower 数据估算，灵犀互娱旗下核心产品《三国志·战略版》9月收入约1600万美元，环比增长54%。中国大陆仍是该游戏的核心收入市场。9月19日，游戏在中国大陆开启七周年庆，活动上线初期收入表现较突出，推动游戏于9月19日至20日连续两日跻身中国大陆 iOS 手游畅销榜第3名，日流水创历年周年庆之最。
哔哩哔哩 旗下新游《闪耀吧！噜咪》（Lumi Master）于9月上线全球市场，该游戏以轻量化捉宠为核心，融合宠物收集养成、策略对战与家园经营。全球市场方面，中国大陆 iOS 贡献游戏约40%的收入，美国和日本合计占约30%，构成主要收入来源。上线后，《闪耀吧！噜咪》迅速升至哔哩哔哩旗下手游9月收入第二名，成为推动发行商收入增长的重要产品。
Joy Games 9月手游收入环比增长30%，主要受《Duck Survival》推动。该作是一款融合割草 Roguelike 战斗、角色养成与基地建设的末日生存手游，Android 早期测试可追溯至2025年4月，国际版 iOS 于2026年5月上线。根据 Sensor Tower 数据估算，9月该游戏环比增长140%，首次超越《菇勇者传说》（Legend of Mushroom），成为该发行商月度收入最高游戏。
益世界 9月发行商收入创历史新高，《疯狂水世界》（Wild Water World）成为关键增量来源。该游戏融合海上生存、资源经营与SLG玩法，中文版于2026年1月上线后收入持续增长，9月突破历史纪录。与此同时，游戏出海表现亮眼，自8月底上市后陆续夺得韩国、中国台湾和日本市场iOS手游下载榜冠军，出海收入快速提升，9月已达到全球收入的60%，并推动其9月收入超过《Lands of Jail》，成为益世界当月收入最高的手游。

中国手游发行商收入TOP 30
9月，中国 App Store 手游收入榜呈现多品类增长态势。腾讯继续占据头部位置，旗下产品包揽榜单前五。其中，自走棋赛道表现突出，《金铲铲之战》受五周年庆典及赛季活动推动，排名升至第4名；新游《王者万象棋》首月进入 App Store 收入榜第11名。与此同时，版本更新与周年庆活动带动多款长线产品收入回升，《原神》收入环比增长42%，重返前十；《阴阳师》迎来十周年庆典，收入环比大涨超170%。
腾讯旗下《金铲铲之战》9月中国大陆 iOS 收入环比增长45%。运营方面，游戏围绕五周年庆典推出系列福利活动，并在“画之灵”赛季返场期间上线限定角色、收藏内容及召唤优惠，形成连续付费节点。根据 Sensor Tower 数据估算，9月30日，游戏升至中国 iOS 手游畅销榜第2名；当日中国大陆 iOS 收入超720万美元，刷新单日收入纪录。
9月，网易旗下《阴阳师》迎来十周年庆典，本期中国大陆收入环比增长超170%，月收入创近3年高峰。9月9日，“永恒庆典”活动开启，推出SSR石长姬、SP百羽凤凰火及登录领100抽等福利，推动游戏升至中国大陆 App Store 畅销榜第3，为年内最佳排名。
腾讯旗下《王者万象棋》9月正式上线，首月即进入中国大陆 App Store 手游收入榜第11名，并连续稳居大陆 iOS 手游免费榜冠军。作为《王者荣耀》IP 衍生产品，游戏在六人自走棋基础上加入竞拍、事件卡与英雄成长机制，与《金铲铲之战》形成玩法差异。根据 Sensor Tower 9月全球自走棋手游收入排名，腾讯旗下两款产品分列前两位，显示其已形成覆盖不同玩法体验的双产品布局，也进一步巩固了在该细分品类的竞争优势。
9月，《原神》位列榜单第9名，排名前进4位。9月23日，7.1版本“往冥府的安魂歌”上线，新五星角色薇斯纳与沃雅妮莎进入上半卡池，为玩家提供了新的角色收集与培养目标。六周年庆同步开启，邮件赠送1600原石及限定五星自选，有效拉动了回流与付费转化。版本更新与周年福利叠加，推动游戏在中国iOS手游畅销榜排名从29位跃升至第2位，单日收入达到年内峰值。
